title: Add interactive migration pauser and cluster compatibility checker
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Summary: Adds an interactive migration pauser controller and a cluster compatibility checker used by the private installer preflight to prevent unsafe upgrades or downgrades. Motivation: we observed two incidents where a schema migration applied during a cluster upgrade caused tenant-level restore failures during rollbacks. This PR introduces runtime protections and deterministic checks that reduce blast radius for in-place upgrades and make automated/machine-driven restores safer.

What this PR does (single-flow): 1) Introduces a lightweight controller (installer/migrationpauser) that can insert a per-upgrade pause point. The controller exposes a CRD MigrationPause that operators can create to halt the installer rollout between helm upgrade hooks and final migration application. Pause points are idempotent and time-limited by default (72h) so a forgotten pause does not block indefinitely. 2) Adds a cluster compatibility checker (cmd/preflight) invoked by the installer and the Terraform module as an optional preflight step. The checker performs: Helm values compatibility checks, a dry-run of kube manifests in a sandbox namespace, and a schema migration dry-run against a read-replica using pg_dump/pg_restore --schema-only mode to detect incompatible DDL (example: dropped columns used by older server components). 3) Adds a restore-verify helm hook that captures restore artifacts and performs an automated verification on a small sample dataset (post-upgrade cannot proceed unless sample restore passes or operator overrides). 4) Adds a version-lockfile (installer/version-lock.yaml) emitted by the build and consumed by the installer to pin chart / module / image checksums used in the upgrade path to make downgrade detection deterministic. 5) Terraform changes add a data source that validates backup object-store URIs and a new module output that surfaces last-successful-snapshot metadata for use in rollout playbooks.

Files touched at a high level: - charts/redwood-private/templates/migration-pause-crd.yaml - charts/redwood-private/templates/restore-verify-hook.yaml - terraform/modules/installer/main.tf - terraform/modules/installer/outputs.tf - cmd/preflight/main.go - cmd/preflight/checker/compatibility.go - tools/backup/verify.go - installer/version-lock.yaml - docs/operational/upgrade-playbook.md - e2e/tests/upgrade_pause_test.go - tests/fixtures/sample_restore.sql - scripts/ci/run-preflight.sh

Testing and verification: Unit tests added for the Compatibility checker (checker unit suite). Integration smoke e2e added to run in CI staging: the test creates a sandbox namespace, applies a canary upgrade with MigrationPause CRD, exercises backup/restore sample verify, and validates that the installer respects the pause until the restore-verify step succeeds. CI: initial run had a flaky e2e due to timing in the fake-pg replica; flake fixed by retry/backoff in e2e harness. Final CI status: pass.

Migration/rollback story and operator experience: - Normal upgrade: installer runs preflight -> compatibility check passes -> helm upgrade runs -> migrations applied -> restore-verify hook executes -> finalization. - If compatibility check fails: installer aborts early and prints remediation hints and a generated remediation.yml with suggested steps. - If restore-verify fails during upgrade: rollout pauses and sets MigrationPause. Operator receives a short checklist via console/CLI with commands to collect debug artifacts and to trigger manual rollback or accept risk and continue. - For rollback safety: version-lockfile prevents accidental reapplication of mismatched charts/images; restore verification ensures backups are restorable before finalizing.

Checklist (what I did): - [x] Implement MigrationPause CRD and controller with default TTL and idempotency. - [x] Implement compatibility checker with Helm dry-run and schema dry-run. - [x] Add restore-verify helm hook and sample verification logic. - [x] Hook Terraform module to surface last-successful-snapshot metadata. - [x] Emit and consume version-lockfile during installer flow. - [x] Unit tests + e2e integration test in staging. - [x] Docs: upgrade-playbook and operator runbook.

Rollout plan: merge to main, ship alpha toggle (installer flag --enable-migration-pauser default false) for one week to low-traffic customers, exercise with Dedicated staging clusters, then flip default to enabled after validating no false-positives for two weekly upgrades.

Risks and mitigations: - False positives in schema dry-run: addressed by limiting to schema-only dry-run and sampling key tables; operators can opt out per-tenant. - Added complexity to installer flow: we gate the feature behind a flag and default TTL to avoid deadlocks. - Restore-verify runtime cost: verification works on a sample dataset by default; full restores still possible via manual path.

Related: ENG-8421 (upgrade incidents), ENG-9145 (restore resilience), SUP-3317 (customer report).
commits:
1) add migration pause CRD and controller with TTL semantics
2) compatibility checker: helm dry-run + schema dry-run implementation
3) restore-verify helm hook + sample verify logic
4) terraform: expose last_successful_snapshot and object_store validation
5) add version-lockfile and installer consumption path
6) e2e: upgrade_pause_test + CI retries for fake-pg
7) docs: operational upgrade playbook and runbook
review_thread:
Aditi Rao: Please add an e2e for the case where the compatibility checker returns a false-positive; how can an operator override safely?
Author (Marisol): Added an operator override flag --force-continue with explicit interactive confirmation and an audit log entry. Also added an example remediation.yml describing safe follow-ups.
Benji Kim: The helm hook looks good but we should ensure post-install hooks don't extend PVC lifetime unexpectedly. Can we scope restore-verify to ephemeral PVCs?
Author: restore-verify uses ephemeral PVCs bound to the sandbox namespace and cleans up with finalizer; added a unit test to assert cleanup.
Lars Engel: Approve after minor docs clarification on TTL semantics.
Aditi Rao: Approve.
CI: one flaky e2e initially failed (timeout against fake-pg replica), retried and passed. All checks green.
release_notes: Adds installer safeguards for in-place migrations: MigrationPause CRD (operator pause points), compatibility preflight checker (helm + schema dry-run), restore-verify helm hook, and version-lockfile support. Feature gated behind --enable-migration-pauser. Recommended to enable in staging first.
notes_for_oncall: If an upgrade is paused with MigrationPause set, do not manually delete the CRD until backups are validated. Use 'redwood-installer preflight --remediation <remediation.yml>' to get suggested steps. Contact Delivery if restore-verify indicates missing snapshots.
